This PR should now only include changes that clean up FanSensor handling for everyone without actually affecting any fan functionality.

A child PR to this one adds the logic change required to support Tachless fan sensors in just a few lines -- but I thought it would easier to review if I kept this first part as free as possible of logic changes.

And a child PR to *that* aims to depreciate the need for distinguishing between non-i2c fans like AspeedFan or HpeFan. Based on ideas & code Ed T had worked on previous.

I'll probably be pushing on this more next week on Discord :)

Added some additional commentary around some usages of 'pwm' and 'pwmPath' that are *not* affected by the fanN_input -> pwmN change here.

Just looking to cover some bases on why some changes were made (or not made).

I've realized this change would break 1:many pwm:tach configurations as coded today. 

I'm going to rethink that part of my approach.

I'm polishing things up now, but the new method should be even simpler to review, and less potential for disruption.

The old method changed all fans over to starting from 'hwmon/pwm' instea of 'hwmon/fan_input' -- but it turns out that would break handling for 1:many pwm:tach configurations.

The new method simply adds 'hwmon/pwm' to the lookup path, then discards any 'pwm' node that isn't isn't tachless, preserving existing behavior for all 'standard' (not tachless) hwmon fans.

The changeover from relying on fanN_input -> pwmN here affects the contents of 'paths/fanOutputPaths' -- meaning it'll start with a list of hwmon paths containing pwmN handles and work from there.

This will not affect fan functionality.
Done. No longer applies.
Refactoring ambiguous 'path' variable names to reflect how they're being used since the switch to starting fan checks from hwmon/pwmN instead of hwmon/fanN_input
Done

Used at the start of the ": fanOutputPaths" loop to identify hwmon sub-directories with fan-associated nodes inside.

This change allows us to start scanning from file 'hwmon/pwmN' (all hwmon-controllable fans should have this) instead of from 'fanN_input' (not all fans expose this).

String manipulation logic has been adjusted accordingly, and all objects are ultimately being passed the same paths as before -- it's should be easier to follow the code now.
Original comment no longer applies.

instead of path manipulation going from fanN_input -> fanN_enable, we now go from pwmN -> fanN_enable

Does not affect fan functionality.
Done. No longer applies.

Handles path string manipulation from hwmon/pwmN -> hwmon/fanN_input.

Needed so we can continue to pass the usual 'fanN_input' path(s) for TachSensor object init.

No changes to any fan functions expected as a result of this change.
Done. No longer applies.

I don't think pwm* index map to the fan*_input index for fan sensors all the time. In our platform, "Pwm" sometimes differs from "Index" of a fan sensor config. This inferring would break those config.

Great point. I think this particular issue might solved by taking the 'index' value from the associated fan EntityManager record and using it here... 

but while I was thinking about that, I realized that my current changes would also break fans for situations with 1 pwm for control, but multiple tach sensors.

So that's something else for me to think about before my next update. Thanks for the help!

In the new version, all hwmon fans with fanN_input nodes are handled like they were originally (back to starting searches with 'fanN_input') -- so breaking support for these fans should no longer be a worry.

I thought about how the index issue you mentioned would work for a tachless fan, and for now, the recommendation is to set 'index=n' and 'pwm=n' in the same EntityManager fan record in order to support a tachless fan with index=n.

For now, we assume if there is a FanN_enable record, it'll match that n. Again, this bit of logic only applies to tachless fans, which have no fanN_input nodes.
How about pwmPaths for clarity?
Acknowledged
I thought this new statement made more sense since we're starting our checks from a fan control/output path (pwmN) now.
Done. No longer applies.
the modified regex from above is now used to match an output path (pwmN) instead of starting from an input path (fanN_input)
Done. No longer applies.

With this change, you are mapping sysfs pwm* index with "Index" property in the config, which is supposed to be mapped to fan*_input index.

Instead of treating this loop as a fan sensor config parsing, I recommend treating this as pwm sensor config parsing, and refactor the loop to cover this change.
Good point. I'll keep this in mind for my next update (which will probably change things around a fair bit, now that I'm thinking about 1:many pwm:tach relationships too...)

After the latest change, only tachless fans will need to worry about potential issues with pwm# != index# -- and I think I've got that solved out too.

My thinking is that tachless fans have no fanN_input records, so they use pwmN nodes as a 'virtual tach input' for PID control to work with. Since that's the case, the pwm index N should always be == the 'virtual tach' index N for tachless fans. 

...With that in mind, setting 'index=N' and 'pwm=N' in EntityManager fan config records gets tachless fans working, and I think makes sense conceptually.

This is a sanity check whose logic is not affected by the hwmon/fanN_input -> hwmon/pwmN changeover.

It essentially checks "does the sensorConfiguration (Entity-Manager config fan record) path have a pwmN index that matches a hwmon/pwmN node that exists? If no, skip to next record.

The result of the sanity check is later used to handle for fans with pwm control, but no 'pwm sensor' offered.

It's likely I could simplify the logic if this PR is accepted, but it'd be a separate PR for discussion, since it may end up adjusting more than just simple string/path logic.
Done. No longer applies.
we still want a fan sensor input path in the end to pass to TachSensor init, so we get it here.
How do we assure that this fan path exist in sysfs? I see your next patch and I do think it should be within this patch to avoid impacts to normal fan configs.
Acknowledged
Done. No longer applies.

The 'pwmPath' logic below is not affected by the changeover to starting from path hwmon/pwmN instead of hwmon/fanN_input.

My understanding is  that this handles cases where Entity-Manager config records defined info for fan pwm control, but not pwm sensor info for lookup.

I suspect the logic could be simplified here, but as it's a parallel hwmon/pwmN lookup that uses the result in interesting ways, I'll see if this PR is successful before trying to touch up the (ain't broke) logic there.

Done. Comment no longer directly applies to the simplified code...

All previous existing fan_input based fans will continue to work like they did before.
tachless-fan or otherwise, the result is a path ending with 'fanN_enable' -- same as before.

We now check for hwmon/pwm# files here too-- but we'll do another check below that allows us to discard any pwm nodes for non-tachless fans. 

This preserves existing behavior for fans with tachs (most of them).

Below is the code this loop used to start off with.

Above is newly added code to discard any 'pwm' paths that aren't associated with tachless fan HW (which keeps behavior the same as it was previously for 'normal' hwmon fan with a tach sensor)

Huh. I didn't realize I had the ability to +2 this PR with a click... Rolling my self-vote back down to a +1 for now :)

The new fix is pretty simple, it's confirmed working with tachless fans (HPE fans), and is not expected to interfere with how standard fans are handled.
All maintainers can +2 anything, it's expected (and enforced at merge time) that they only +2 the things for which they have permissions.  All good, just FYI.

Before this update, filename could only be 'fanN_input.' After the update, the filename can be 'fanN_input' OR 'pwmN'.

This check here lets us filter out those newly-included pwmN paths for all standard (non-tachless) fans. After this point, everything is 'business as usual' for standard fans, with 'isTachlessFan' checks gating any tachless-specific path-string manipulations as needed.
enableFanInput behavior is unchanged for standard (non-tachless) fans.

I'm not a huge fan of adding more regexes here.  std::regex is crazy expensive to build and not the fastest in the std implementation.  We had it here before, so I'm not that worried about it, but lets not propagate it as a "good" pattern.  Probably just a simple helper with a prefix match and a from_chars would be a lot faster.
Overall in support of this.

As written, this extends the function to ~roughly~ `707-320 = 387` lines.

It was horrible before, and this patch does not make it better.

Let's stack a series to get it cleaned up by successively extracting functions.

After that's done let's stack this patch on top.

As per core guidelines:

https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#f3-keep-functions-short-and-simple

I'm aware that it should not be your job to clean up behind other people but i don't see us extending this function any further.
Please make this a group.  (pwm\d+)|(fan\d+_input)
Should this just be handled within "isTachless"?
This really should be matching on fanNodePath.filename(), and doing a regex_match not a regex_search, to avoid surprises of files or folders that might share names.
This function is already massive.  Lets make sure we're not making the problem worse here.
